subject: Word Power

assessment.name: Year 8 vocabulary builder
assessment.sections: Fill-the-gap mock: choose the word that fits each sentence. Practise 10 words a day.
assessment.weighting: Six word groups linked to Year 8 English, History, Science and Geography, and the Year 8 reading canon.

mock.note: 20 fill-the-gap sentences. Read the whole sentence before choosing.

how_to_use: Say the word, read the meaning, then cover it and use the word in your own sentence.
Learn the memory hook. Hooks link the word to a picture or a word you already know.
Use two new words in every piece of writing this week, in any subject.

written.q: Write a short paragraph arguing that your school should plant more trees. Use at least four words from Arguing and persuading.
Describe an old empty house at night in 4 to 6 sentences. Use at least four words from Gothic and atmosphere.
Describe how Juliet changes during Romeo and Juliet, using at least three words from Character and emotion.

exam_tips.timing: 10 words a day, 10 minutes a day.
section_a: Read the whole sentence before choosing a word.
Check the word class. A gap before a noun often needs an adjective.
section_b: Use each new word in your own sentence within 24 hours.
Swap a plain word (bad, sad, big) for a precise one every time you redraft.
week: Most days, 10 minutes: 10 words in Flashcards.
Once a week: use three of this week's words in sentences about your own day, out loud or written.
Once a week: the fill-the-gap mock test.
Fix one mistake: write the word you missed in a new sentence of your own.

vocab.meaning: To publicly support or speak up for an idea
vocab.example: Greta Thunberg continues to advocate for urgent action on climate change.
vocab.hook: An advocate adds a VOICE (voc = voice in Latin) to a cause.

vocab.meaning: So strong or interesting that it convinces you
vocab.example: The writer gives a compelling reason to recycle.
vocab.hook: Compel = force: a compelling argument forces you to agree.

vocab.meaning: To argue that something is true
vocab.example: Some people contend that one person cannot change the climate.
vocab.hook: Contenders compete; to contend is to compete with an argument.

vocab.meaning: Extremely important
vocab.example: Cutting carbon emissions is crucial for our future.
vocab.hook: Crucial sounds like crux: the central point.

vocab.meaning: To weaken something gradually
vocab.example: Littering can undermine the effort to keep our parks clean.
vocab.hook: Under + mine: digging under a wall makes it fall.

vocab.meaning: To give special importance to something
vocab.example: Use short sentences to emphasise your strongest point.
vocab.hook: Emphasis is the bold, underlined bit.

vocab.meaning: To give good reasons for something
vocab.example: Always justify your opinion with evidence.
vocab.hook: Justify = make it just (fair).

vocab.meaning: To prove an argument wrong
vocab.example: Use clear facts to refute the other side's claim.
vocab.hook: Refute = rebut: refuse to accept the argument.

vocab.meaning: Suggesting something bad is about to happen
vocab.example: An ominous mist crept across the marshes in The Woman in Black.
vocab.hook: Ominous has omen in it: a sign of bad things.

vocab.meaning: Empty, bleak and lonely
vocab.example: Eel Marsh House stands in a desolate landscape.
vocab.hook: De + solus (alone): left all alone.

vocab.meaning: Strange and frightening
vocab.example: An eerie silence filled the empty nursery.
vocab.hook: Eerie sounds like ear-ie: you strain your ears in the silence.

vocab.meaning: A feeling that something bad will happen
vocab.example: Arthur felt a deep foreboding as the fog rolled in.
vocab.hook: Fore = before: you feel the bad thing before it comes.

vocab.meaning: Threatening harm
vocab.example: A menacing figure in black appeared at the funeral.
vocab.hook: A menace is a threat.

vocab.meaning: Far away from others
vocab.example: The house is isolated when the tide covers the causeway.
vocab.hook: Isola = island in Italian: alone like an island.

vocab.meaning: Great fear about something that will happen
vocab.example: He walked back to the house with growing dread.
vocab.hook: Dread rhymes with the dead: what you fear.

vocab.meaning: To cover and hide something
vocab.example: Thick fog began to shroud the marsh.
vocab.hook: A shroud is a cloth that covers a body.

vocab.meaning: Acting quickly without thinking
vocab.example: Romeo's impetuous decision to marry Juliet leads to disaster.
vocab.hook: Impetuous has impetus: full speed ahead.

vocab.meaning: Openly refusing to obey
vocab.example: Juliet becomes defiant when her father demands she marry Paris.
vocab.hook: Defiant = defies: stands against.

vocab.meaning: Able to recover quickly from difficulty
vocab.example: The boys in Cane Warriors are resilient in the face of cruelty.
vocab.hook: Resilient = bounces back like a spring.

vocab.meaning: Deeply and thoughtfully sad
vocab.example: At the start, Romeo is melancholy over Rosaline.
vocab.hook: Melan = black in Greek: a dark mood.

vocab.meaning: Wanting to get revenge
vocab.example: Tybalt is vengeful after Romeo comes to the party.
vocab.hook: Vengeful = full of vengeance.

vocab.meaning: Faithful and supportive
vocab.example: Mercutio is loyal to Romeo until the end.
vocab.hook: Loyal sounds like royal: loyal to the king.

vocab.meaning: Severe pain or suffering, often of the mind
vocab.example: Juliet's anguish grows when Romeo is banished.
vocab.hook: Anguish comes from the Latin for tightness: a tight, painful feeling.

vocab.meaning: Showing care for others who suffer
vocab.example: The Friar is compassionate but his plan fails.
vocab.hook: Com + passion: feeling with someone.

vocab.meaning: The power to give orders
vocab.example: King Charles I believed his authority came from God.
vocab.hook: Author: the one who writes the rules.

vocab.meaning: Fighting against those in power
vocab.example: The enslaved rebels in Cane Warriors plan a rebellion.
vocab.hook: Re + bellum (war): going to war again against rulers.

vocab.meaning: To treat people cruelly, often for their beliefs
vocab.example: Puritans believed the bishops wanted to persecute them.
vocab.hook: Persecute ≠ prosecute: persecute means pick on.

vocab.meaning: Cruel and unfair use of power
vocab.example: Parliament accused Charles I of tyranny.
vocab.hook: Tyranny has a T-Rex in it: a cruel ruler.

vocab.meaning: An agreement to work together
vocab.example: Charles I married a French princess to build an alliance.
vocab.hook: Alliance = allies together.

vocab.meaning: A change to improve something
vocab.example: Puritans wanted further reform of the Church.
vocab.hook: Re + form: form it again, better.

vocab.meaning: A king or queen with supreme power
vocab.example: The Oba of Benin was a powerful sovereign.
vocab.hook: Sovereign contains reign.

vocab.meaning: Disagreement with official views
vocab.example: Charles I dissolved Parliament to silence dissent.
vocab.hook: Dis + sent: you send back a different view.

vocab.meaning: An idea that can be tested
vocab.example: Our hypothesis was that pressure increases with depth.
vocab.hook: Hypo = under, thesis = idea: the idea under the test.

vocab.meaning: Facts that show something is true
vocab.example: Limewater turning milky is evidence of carbon dioxide.
vocab.hook: Evident = easy to see.

vocab.meaning: To decide after looking at the evidence
vocab.example: We can conclude that acids have a pH below 7.
vocab.hook: Conclude = close the case.

vocab.meaning: Correct and close to the true value
vocab.example: An accurate thermometer shows the true temperature.
vocab.hook: Accurate = acc-u-rate: rate it right.

vocab.meaning: Absolutely necessary for life or success
vocab.example: Kay's Anatomy explains that the heart is vital for life.
vocab.hook: Vita = life in Latin.

vocab.meaning: The job something does
vocab.example: The function of the alveoli is gas exchange.
vocab.hook: Function = what it does.

vocab.meaning: To watch carefully
vocab.example: Observe the colour change in the indicator.
vocab.hook: Observatory: where we watch the stars.

vocab.meaning: To change completely
vocab.example: Chemical reactions transform reactants into products.
vocab.hook: Trans = across: across to a new form.

vocab.meaning: In short supply
vocab.example: Water becomes scarce during a drought.
vocab.hook: Scarce sounds like scared: scared there will not be enough.

vocab.meaning: Able to continue without harming the future
vocab.example: William built a sustainable windmill from scrap in The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind.
vocab.hook: Sustain = keep going.

vocab.meaning: Easily harmed
vocab.example: Families who depend on one crop are vulnerable to famine.
vocab.hook: Vulner = wound in Latin: easily wounded.

vocab.meaning: Able to grow plenty of crops
vocab.example: The floodplain of the Nile is very fertile.
vocab.hook: Fertile soil: fertiliser makes it fertile.

vocab.meaning: A long period with little or no rain
vocab.example: A drought destroyed the maize harvest in Malawi.
vocab.hook: Drought rhymes with out: the water has run out.

vocab.meaning: To change to suit new conditions
vocab.example: Farmers adapt by growing crops that need less water.
vocab.hook: Ad + apt (fit): change to fit.

vocab.meaning: A result of an action
vocab.example: Famine is one consequence of crop failure.
vocab.hook: Con + sequence: what comes next in the sequence.

vocab.meaning: To create new ideas or methods
vocab.example: William Kamkwamba showed that young people can innovate.
vocab.hook: Nova = new.
